topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This opening frames the lecture within the series and introduces its intended learning outcomes.

topics.label: Mutation accumulation and clonal selection
topics.groupedBecause: These explanations and experiments establish how mutations give cell clones selective advantages during cancer evolution.

topics.label: Epigenetic disruption as a driver of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: This material examines how altered transcriptional accessibility can initiate tumor development without additional mutations.

topics.label: Cell of origin and cancer stem cell models
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how a cell's position in a tissue hierarchy and its capacity for self-renewal influence tumor initiation and propagation.

topics.label: Inflammation-induced stemness in cancer initiation
topics.groupedBecause: Both cancer models show how inflammatory signals can confer stem-like properties that enable previously nonmalignant mutant cells to develop tumors.

topics.label: Microenvironmental support of established tumors
topics.groupedBecause: This material explains established tumors' dependence on supportive surrounding cells and how that dependence creates therapeutic opportunities.

topics.label: Single-cell and spatial methods for studying cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These approaches reveal cancer evolution and cellular interactions by resolving molecular states within individual cells and tissue locations.

topics.label: Converging conditions for malignant evolution
topics.groupedBecause: This synthesis explains how malignancy depends on favorable conditions coinciding, extending that argument to developmental susceptibility and tumor–microenvironment coevolution.

topics.label: Lecture close and next session
topics.groupedBecause: This closing ends the lecture and announces the forthcoming session on therapy.
